cells.tense: You sit here at the table with the pen in your hand and nothing needing it yet.
cells.act: set one rule that makes the rest easier
cells.ask: Set one rule — a single line you can keep — that makes everything around it easier to carry. Not a system to maintain, just the line, somewhere you'll see it.
cells.core:
You know what needs your attention long before you can say how you know. It shows up in small choices: which person to call, which page to open, which conversation can wait. The reasoning is seldom in place first, and when a structure around you comes apart, you're steady in it, because you could see it wouldn't hold. That's the shape of it when it's going well — clear ground under you, no argument needed.

What you haven't done is give that clear ground a shape. Set one rule — a single line you can keep — that makes everything around it easier to carry. Not a system to maintain, just the line, somewhere you'll see it. It gives the next thing somewhere to land, and it lets the clear ground last longer than the week.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters. Give it a line to stand on.
cells.place: where a structure that could not hold comes down

cells.tense: The whole collapse is being prepared for in advance, and no part of it has arrived yet.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Name what you actually want, the thing whose loss would cost most, and turn toward it once — one small move, plainly, without explaining it to anyone.
cells.core:
You can feel a structure coming down before it does, and you're getting ahead of it, cataloguing everything that might be needed so nothing catches you. Gathering was knowing once. Now nothing gets in without being checked first, and the thing you actually care about sits behind the checking. That's the shape of it when it's going well — you can want something without a file on it.

Name what you actually want, the thing whose loss would cost most, and turn toward it once — one small move, plainly, without explaining it to anyone. You don't need the whole picture. Wanting it is already the direction.
cells.sheetLine: You know the structure is going. You're cataloguing, not leaving.

cells.tense: The clearing already happened behind you, and you are still standing at the door checking it.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Take the next small step with only the light you have now, without asking anyone to confirm it or waiting until the road is clear.
cells.core:
Something you trusted about your own seeing stopped, and you've been asking the outside what to do ever since — one more confirmation, one more sign-off from someone who might know. What's missing is the confirmer, not the knowledge. This is the shape of it when it's going well: the perception lands and you don't argue with it.

Take the next small step with only the light you have now, without asking anyone to confirm it or waiting until the road is clear. You'll be moving with most of it dark, and the ground will hold the one step you're on — that's all the ground you've ever needed.
cells.sheetLine: The road is clear. You're asking the outside if it's clear.

cells.tense: You are writing this with the pen already down, crediting the paper instead of your hand.
cells.act: put it in proportion, not in punishment
cells.ask: Look at a choice you've been calling random — the job, the move, the person you keep choosing — and name what you saw. To yourself, once. No debt owed, no punishment, just what was already operating.
cells.core:
You keep making calls that turn out right, and you chalk them up to luck, or a hunch, or the timing working out. The perceiving was yours. You haven't been discrediting it out of modesty — you've been mis-crediting it, which is a different thing, and it leaves your own perception off the record.

Look at a choice you've been calling random — the job, the move, the person you keep choosing — and name what you saw. To yourself, once. No debt owed, no punishment, just what was already operating. The structure is coming down either way. It comes down better when you know whose call it was the last time.
cells.sheetLine: You say it was random. You were the one seeing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's surroundings — a group, a plan, old premises — are actually false. The record says the seat is false structure collapsing, not that the person knows it is false. The reader could rightly say none of it was fake, only that it stopped holding, so each core keeps the collapse as something already underway or nearly so, described in the person's terms, with no verdict on the structure's truth. The asks survive being wrong because each is a small act of structure or orientation the person can use whether or not the read lands. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'what you knew before you understood why' — it is too neat and it credits the person for a story instead of handing them an act, so it gets trimmed or left out.
